ui.printstage.title: Lay things out on your printer’s bed and send them to the printer
ps.title: Print stage
ps.lab: New in this build. Watch the first prints: this slicer has not yet been tried on many printers.
ps.lib.none: Nothing in the Library matches that.
ps.lib.failed: The Library could not be reached.
ps.add.nobody: This item has no 3D shape to print.
ps.add.failed: This item could not be added.
ps.add.done: {name} is on the bed at full size.
ps.add.scaled: {name} is on the bed at 1:{n} so it fits.
ps.stage.empty: Nothing here yet. Add something from the Library, or draw or import a model: everything shown in the view prints.
ps.stage.move: Move, rotate and scale things in the view with the usual tools. The dashed outline is your bed.
ps.stage.overlap: Some boxes overlap. That is fine if the shapes do not touch; shapes that do touch print as one piece.
ps.arrange.left: {n} did not fit. Scale them down or print them in another run.
ps.link.needs_studio: This printer works from CadCraft Studio on a computer. Open this model in Studio to send it.
ps.link.slicer: This printer uses OrcaSlicer with its own presets. Material, quality, infill and supports below still apply; temperatures come from the preset.
ps.engine.need.needs_studio: {name} is a program of its own, so it works from CadCraft Studio on a computer. Pick another slicer here, or open this in Studio.
ps.engine.need.not_found: {name} was not found on this computer.
ps.engine.need.too_old: This copy of {name} is too old.
ps.tech.label: Printing with
ps.printer.mk4: Prusa MK4 style, 250 × 210 × 220 mm (own start G-code)
ps.field.bridges: Bridge gaps (printed across, slower, fan full)
ps.preview.ready: Sliced: {n} layers. Move the slider to look through them before you send.
ps.preview.canvas: The sliced layer seen from above, on the outline of the bed
ps.preview.stale: The stage or the settings changed since this was sliced. Press Preview layers again.
ps.usb.none: USB printing needs Chrome or Edge on a computer. A network printer works from here too.
ps.net.note: The printer has to allow this site. In Moonraker, add this site to cors_domains; in OctoPrint, turn on CORS and copy an API key. Your browser may ask to reach devices on your network: say yes.
ps.send.empty: There is nothing on the bed to print.
ps.send.off: Move these onto the bed first: {names}.
ps.send.check: Is the bed clear, and the right material loaded? The printer will heat up and start moving.
ps.send.summary: About {time}, {grams} g of material, {layers} layers. Nozzle {temp} °C, bed {bed} °C.
ps.send.usb_note: Over USB, keep this page open until the print ends. Closing it stops the stream, and the heaters stay on until the printer times out.
ps.send.started: Sent. The printer is starting: about {time}.
ps.send.usb_done: Everything was sent and the print has finished.
ps.send.stopped: Stopped. Heaters, fan and motors are off.
ps.warn.skipped_one: One piece has no thickness or could not be closed, so it will be missing ({share}% of the shape).
ps.warn.skipped: {n} pieces have no thickness or could not be closed, so they will be missing ({share}% of the shape).
ps.warn.sheets_one: One flat panel (a label or trim line) had no thickness, so it was printed one nozzle line thick.
ps.warn.sheets: {n} flat panels (labels or trim lines) had no thickness, so they were printed one nozzle line thick.
ps.warn.thin: Up to {n}% of a layer is too thin for this nozzle and will not print. Make it bigger, or thicken those parts.
ps.warn.overhang: Some parts have nothing under them. Turn on supports, or turn the model so they do.
ps.warn.floating: The model did not sit on the bed, so it was moved down to it.
ps.slice.open: None of this is a closed shape, so there is nothing a printer can fill.
ps.slice.bed: This does not fit on the bed. Use Fit all on the bed, or move it inside the outline.
ps.slice.failed: The print could not be prepared.
ps.fail.unreachable: The printer did not answer. Check the address, that it allows this site, and that your browser may reach your network.
ps.fail.key: The printer refused the API key.
ps.fail.busy: The printer is busy with another print.
ps.fail.unsupported: This browser cannot use USB devices.
ps.fail.printer: The printer reported an error, so sending stopped.
ps.pc.pick: Pick one thing on the list below to turn it.
ps.pc.flat.title: Put the largest flat face that can carry it on the bed
ps.pc.turn.title: Turn it a quarter turn on the bed
ps.pc.asdesigned.title: Put it back the way the part is drawn (its up is up)
ps.pc.flat.done: {name} lies on a flat face of {area} mm².
ps.pc.flat.already: {name} already lies on its largest flat face.
ps.pc.flat.none: {name} has no flat face to rest on. Turn it by hand.
ps.pc.why.open: it has {n} open edges, so its skin has holes
ps.pc.why.nonmanifold: it has {n} edges where three or more faces meet
ps.pc.why.flipped: it has {n} places where neighbouring faces point opposite ways
ps.pc.why.selfintersect: it passes through itself in {n} places
ps.bim.note: Pick elements in the 3D view, then take them. They lie on the bed as copies, with their placements as drawn. Moving, turning and scaling them here changes the print layout only, never the model.
ps.bim.take.sel.title: Put the elements picked in the 3D view on the bed
ps.bim.take.shown.title: Put every element the 3D view shows on the bed (at most 300)
ps.bim.none.sel: Nothing is picked in the 3D view. Pick elements, then take them again.
ps.bim.left: {name} is left off the bed: it is not a closed solid, {why}.
ps.bim.more: {n} more elements were not taken: a bed holds 300 things at most. Pick fewer.
ps.bim.scale.title: Scale everything on the bed by one number, so the proportions stay
ps.bim.lifesize.title: Put everything back at its size in the model (too big for most beds)
ps.bim.lifesized: Everything is at its size in the model again.
